distinct_crash_signature_observed_elsewh.note: An earlier root-cause session (before this closing checkpoint) observed the SAME class of failure manifest as a clean GGML_ASSERT instead of a raw SIGSEGV, in a different scenario (ctx=8192, mode=cycle, repeated CPU<->GPU relocation loop): 'GGML_ASSERT(buffer != nullptr) failed' at third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:7815 (ggml_vk_tensor_subbuffer), backend=Vulkan1, on the llama_decode() call following the second relocation's release. Both signatures indicate the same underlying class of problem (a stale/dangling reference into freed backend memory), not two separate bugs.

non_crashing_counter_example_disclosed_h.note: mode=roundtrip performs the logically identical operation (same layer, CPU->GPU->CPU, old backing release attempted by default) but interleaves generate_greedy(4 tokens) between relocation #1 and relocation #2 (more decode calls than trial_2's settle test, in a different function/call structure) and completed WITHOUT a crash, reproducibly, across 4 repeated runs (see raw_roundtrip_135m_layer4.json, raw_roundtrip_135m_layer4_ctx16384.json). This is explicitly NOT treated as proof that release is safe in that call pattern -- call-pattern-dependent, non-uniform manifestation is the classic signature of a use-after-free/stale-reference bug, and the demonstrated corruption elsewhere in this section means the retained-old-backing path (repeated_same_layer_retained.json) is the only one this phase can certify as safe.

conclusion: Freeing a layer's old dedicated backing on its second (or later) relocation is UNSAFE with the current minimal design -- it reliably crashes in the tested reproducer and its settle-window variant, and remains uncertified even where it appears not to crash. Old backing must be retained (leaked) to keep relocation safe -- see repeated_same_layer_retained.json for the functionally-correct, retained-backing alternative.
